blocks.text: The wish

content.value: W1–W4 are CLOSED and LIVE: a 7-command corpus, bp scaffy validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla as command documents, reversibility proof matrix 6/6 PERFECT (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof). W5 = EXPAND THE CATALOG + STRESS THE GRAMMAR, on three axes.

(1) DISCOVERY — mine what Barkpark development ACTUALLY repeats: git-history co-change mining (files that keep co-changing with revolving siblings = injection candidates; suffix-pair co-creations; directory-shape fingerprints), the Past Mistakes / memory lore (error-shape duplication across query_controller+legacy_controller, layer-parity chores, canonical-marker planting, changeset entries, docs-currency), and the CUT backlog (scaffy-backlog-api-route-parity, scaffy-backlog-add-schema-type — revisit now that marks+REANCHOR exist).

(2) SMALL DELICATE commands — one-op precision tools a developer reaches for daily (ensure-import, add-canonical-marker, add-error-shape FOREACH-over-emitters, add-changeset, add-test-fixture…) — cheap to author, high frequency. (3) COMPREHENSIVE multi-step commands — full vertical slices (new content type end-to-end: schema+Studio+SDK+TUI; new search retriever; new cloud site template; new theme slice) — where the GRAMMAR GAPS live: v2 has NO conditional branches, NO multi-choice/enum variables, NO FOREACH (the Doey-era DSL had one), NO command composition, NO optional op groups.

For each candidate: expressible in TODAY's grammar → author it (validated, anchors live-verified per D5, seeded per D46/D47); needs a NEW primitive → spec the primitive as a ratify-or-reject proposal with the command as motivating fixture (D3/D12/D20–D32 discipline: no primitive without a real command needing it). Deliverables: ranked candidate inventory with frequency×pain evidence; best N commands AUTHORED full-text; grammar-gap verdicts (multi-choice/enum, optional groups, composition — each ratified or rejected with reasoning); showcase/catalog updated. Rounds law: dispatcher consumes round/after natively (d38434b53) — command slices needing a new primitive are round ≥2 behind the primitive, or deferred.

content.value: The finished experience: bp scaffy ls --remote grows from a 7-row proof into a working CATALOG — roughly a dozen-plus commands where every entry answers a repetition the repo can PROVE it has (≥3 historical instances in git history, a Past-Mistakes scar, or a live backlog chore). A developer's daily reflex changes: before hand-editing an accretion file, you check the catalog. And the grammar leaves the wave with an honest verdict sheet: each missing primitive either ratified with a motivating command already written against it, or rejected with the cheaper spelling that makes it unnecessary.

Lean 1 — EVIDENCE BEFORE AUTHORSHIP. The ranked inventory is the wave's spine artifact. Frequency×pain comes from three mines: git co-change clusters, memory/Past-Mistakes lore, and the open backlog. A command nobody would run twice a quarter does not get authored, however elegant.

Lean 2 — SMALL DELICATE COMMANDS ARE THE MEAT. The strongest candidates on current knowledge: add-error-shape (the query_controller+legacy_controller duplication is a documented scar — and it doubles as the FOREACH test case: if the emitter set is closed and small, explicit ops beat a loop primitive), add-canonical-marker (the @canonical planting ritual has exact syntax, a gate — docs-anchors-check §8 — and a grep-index convention), add-oban-cron-guard fix-up, add-test-fixture, ensure-import. Each is 1–3 ops, cheap to author, high frequency. These ship in round 1 in TODAY's grammar.

Lean 3 — COMPREHENSIVE COMMANDS ARE THE STRESS INSTRUMENT, not necessarily shipped verticals. Revisit add-api-route-parity (CUT in W1 for anchor reasons that marks+REANCHOR have since dissolved — the 6-anchors-3-subsystems objection needs re-testing against the W3 engine) and add-schema-type (must wrap or differentiate bp make schema). The full new-content-type vertical is attempted ON PAPER first: walk it op by op until it either fits today's grammar or names the exact primitive it dies without. That named failure IS the deliverable — it becomes the motivating fixture.

Lean 4 — GRAMMAR VERDICT PRIORS (to be tested, not assumed): ONEOF/enum variable constraint looks CHEAP and REAL (validator-level annotation in the D22 family — OPAQUE/SHAPE/SUCCESSOR precedent; add-block-type's block-family choice and add-plugin's capability set both want it); FOREACH looks REJECTABLE if every real emitter-set is closed (explicit ops are more auditable and receipt-replay stays trivial); optional op groups look REJECTABLE on house doctrine (the test is never optional here) unless a real command shows a true optional leg; command composition looks DEFERRABLE (no motivating fixture yet — the comprehensive walk decides). Conditional branches: almost certainly reject — DIRECTION+VARIANT already split polarity and flavor into separate documents, which is the scaffy way.

Lean 5 — ROUNDS HONESTY. Round 1: inventory-driven commands in today's grammar + grammar-law spec slice (if any primitive ratifies). Round 2+: commands that NEED a ratified primitive ride behind the validator/engine change, or defer to W6 entirely. Seeding + showcase update dispatch LAST (D19's lesson: the showcase embeds merged truth, never drafts).

Quality bar: every authored command meets the full W1–W4 law — DIRECTION header, marks payload-planted or VIRTUAL, guards payload-derived, ValidateFile zero findings, fmt fixpoint, anchors grep-proven with file:line evidence, seeded and tokenless-readable on guerrilla, and reversibility demonstrated (receipt replay or authored inverse). content.value: DISCOVERY axis, hard numbers from 12 months / 2874 commits: router.ex is the repo’s top accretion file (739 distinct co-change partners across 173 commits), followed by root.html.heex (501), content.ex (441), studio_live.ex (354), config.exs, application.exs, capabilities.ex, cli.go, types.ts. Suffix-pair co-creation: 295 commits added an .ex module WITH its _test.exs; 157 did .go/_test.go (dominated by internal/cli *_cmd.go — already covered by add-cli-verb). Commit-message corroboration: “canonical” 274 commits, “changeset” 276. Rare and already-covered: plugin registration (max pairwise co-change 5), Oban workers (10 co-adds/12mo). docs/openapi.json’s high partner count is CI churn, not a human chore.

PREMISE CORRECTION 1 — the error-shape scar is ALREADY CENTRALIZED. All 13 controllers fan into FallbackController → Barkpark.Content.Errors (errors.ex, ~35 build/1 clauses); query_controller.ex:35-44 and legacy_controller.ex:45,142 emit the SAME shared tuples, handled by one clause (errors.ex:269-305). The comments in errors.ex document that the bare-map duplication was fixed. A NEW error code touches exactly 4 manual sites (build/1 clause + @hints entry in errors.ex, docs/api-v1.md §9, errors_test.exs) — openapi.ex’s enum and error_code_coverage_test self-derive. Two scouts (co-change mining, reversibility) treated the 2-controller duplication as live pain; the direct module read wins. Consequence: add-error-shape is a closed 4-site command in TODAY’s grammar, and the wish’s FOREACH motivating fixture dissolves.

PREMISE CORRECTION 2 — the Doey-era DSL NEVER had a FOREACH. Full read of nextgen-vscode’s 698-line reference grammar file, the language server’s keyword whitelist (diagnostics.ts:57), and all 9 commits of its git history: zero DSL-level FOREACH (only JS Array.forEach in the extension’s own code). The real inherited scar is the quote-mismatch re-insert bug (charter D3c), already mechanized as E-006. FOREACH’s verdict must stand on today’s cost/benefit alone — and it does: remove/replay is 100% receipt-driven (remove.go:171 replays Receipt.Ops in reverse, never re-reads cmd.Ops), so explicit multi-site ops are independently invertible TODAY; dynamic FOREACH would break D27 (text-only validate) and D33 (static K).

Grammar-gap leans, now evidence-backed. ONEOF/enum variable: CHEAP, ratify-ready — parse.go:361-371 (EXAMPLES comma-list) is the verbatim parser template, subst.go checkShape/checkSuccessor (111-152) the runtime-check precedent, format.go’s joinFields (88-106) is keyword-agnostic so fmt is FREE, D30 bill is 1 red fixture; needs a named motivating fixture command per D22 discipline (candidates: bump-level in add-changeset, visibility in add-schema-type, tier in classify-block-type). Optional op groups: receipt/remove-SAFE by construction (skipped ops never enter the receipt; zero-mutation runs write no receipt) but the real cost is a second block-delimiter type in the parser and format.go’s 2-state fence machine — plus house doctrine (tests are never optional) and no fixture: REJECT lean holds. Composition: every engine layer is closed over ONE source file (singular Command.SourceFile; per-file mark uniqueness E-019; flat receipt schema) — receipt nesting is a schema rewrite, validation would live in the R-xxx repo-aware namespace, and no candidate needs it (add-schema-type can ASSERT the plugin exists as a precondition): DEFER. Conditionals: REJECT (DIRECTION/VARIANT already split polarity/flavor). NEW gap surfaced by the theme-slice walk: a value-capture primitive (read a token from an existing file into a VARIABLE) — real but only 2 instances, below the wave’s own 3+ bar: DEFER, name it in the verdict sheet.

Backlog revisits. add-api-route-parity: 2 of 3 D10 cut reasons hold VERBATIM at HEAD — capabilities.ex:192 still discards collect_routes (dead manifest↔router cross-check) and the 857-line contract test is hand-written per command (no auto-extend). The anchor-count worry (6 anchors / 3 subsystems) is REBUTTED by live precedent: add-block-type ships 6 IN-blocks across Go/Elixir/JS today. But plugin-owned routes AND CLI commands already auto-fold into the manifest with zero hand-edits (router/plugins.ex:177; capabilities.ex:193,230) — so the honest paths are retire-in-favor-of-plugin-register_routes or narrow to one /v1/data-zone method with the JS leg accepted as open; the original “live cross-check” acceptance bar is unmet and is a TARGET-REPO test-infra gap, not a scaffy grammar gap. That named failure is itself a wish deliverable. add-schema-type: verdict DIFFERENTIATE, not wrap — bp make schema is a pure local skeleton emitter for the ad-hoc POST /v1/schemas path, and its output shape (name/title/type:document) does NOT match plugin JSON (name/title/icon/visibility, no type key); the command’s job is the plugin-declared path: CREATE priv/plugins/<n>/schemas/*.json + register_schemas/1 wiring + test, all in today’s grammar. Caveat: tickets/quiz use inline Elixir SchemaDefinition, not JSON files — scope must say so. Correction: the direction’s “D15” cite is the add-plugin/mix-task supersession precedent; it applies to schema-type by analogy only.

New small-delicate candidates beyond the wish’s list (each with live anchors): ensure-cli-noun (3-copy drift: builtins.go:306 completionNouns is tested, the cli.go dispatch switch is D31-known, but usage.go:36 carries a THIRD, untested copy nothing ties back); ensure-cli-flag (capabilities.ex has 90 flag() calls; the missing --file class shipped as real bug #3810 and two open backlog tasks bundle with it); classify-block-type (tiers.ex @element/@widget/@section word-lists — the exact manual step charter D11 says add-block-type must never blind-MARK); add-pd-parity-entry (gen_pd_parity.ex’s @inputs map is untouched by add-block-type — a fresh, grep-proven drift gap; verify pending on whether @inputs is a hand literal); add-backfill-task (8+ Mix.Tasks share a byte-identical dry-run/--apply idiom, e.g. edges.backfill.ex:51 == paper.backfill_block_ids.ex:59 — unfiled anywhere until now); add-retriever (1 behaviour module + 1 config.exs line; registry needs zero edits). LIKELY CUT as scaffy commands: add-changeset and add-test-fixture (CREATE-only, no guarded anchor — scaffy’s MARK/REANCHOR/reversibility machinery buys nothing over a plain template; changesets also have pnpm changeset add), add-site-template (all-CREATE, 10-file stamp; discovery mechanism unverified). Tag-registry chores are live-dataset actions, not file injections — out of scaffy’s domain. No docs-currency accretion file exists (checker scripts only).

Round-0 operational facts. The INSTALLED bp binary is 89 commits stale and lacks scaffy run/remove/pull/ls entirely — make cli-build is a mandatory round-0 step or builders will misdiagnose phantom gaps. All 18 corpus tags are pre-registered on guerrilla, but ANY new tag vocabulary 422s at the publish wall (D47) — the seed slice must pre-register new tags. The serving loop is proven live at HEAD: ls --remote = 7 commands, pull→validate→consent transcript green, reversibility matrix 6/6 confirmed against d38434b53. The charter wave-log is stale (W4 finale + seed-corpus merged after its last edit) and D43/D53 still describe manual round-sequencing — SUPERSEDED: the dispatcher natively consumes round/after since d38434b53 (buildNow = round 1; round≥2 returned as deferred_slices), but it is NOT failure-aware: a red round-1 slice does not auto-cancel its dependent round-2 — Review/lead judgment must catch orphans. Backlog triage of 13 open children: 3 graduate to command candidates (api-route-parity, add-schema-type, oban-cron-guard-gap’s update-variant), 5 are sweep fixes (anchors-omx-exclusion p2, docs-anchors-nm-prune, js-assert-sweep, pnpm-assert-overbroad, file-flag bundle), 5 stay parked.

Scaffy W5 — Expand the Catalog + Stress the Grammar: the wave story

IN FLIGHT: DIGEST done — 11 verifiers flying now (2 Opus worktree probes, 9 Sonnet), the LAST exploration round. Next: Decide consumes the run-proofs, files the W5 goal task + slice tasks under bp-scaffy-epic, and appends decisions here.

The wish

W1–W4 are CLOSED and LIVE: a 7-command corpus, bp scaffy validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla as command documents, reversibility proof matrix 6/6 PERFECT (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof). W5 = EXPAND THE CATALOG + STRESS THE GRAMMAR, on three axes.

(1) DISCOVERY — mine what Barkpark development ACTUALLY repeats: git-history co-change mining (files that keep co-changing with revolving siblings = injection candidates; suffix-pair co-creations; directory-shape fingerprints), the Past Mistakes / memory lore (error-shape duplication across query_controller+legacy_controller, layer-parity chores, canonical-marker planting, changeset entries, docs-currency), and the CUT backlog (scaffy-backlog-api-route-parity, scaffy-backlog-add-schema-type — revisit now that marks+REANCHOR exist).

(2) SMALL DELICATE commands — one-op precision tools a developer reaches for daily (ensure-import, add-canonical-marker, add-error-shape FOREACH-over-emitters, add-changeset, add-test-fixture…) — cheap to author, high frequency. (3) COMPREHENSIVE multi-step commands — full vertical slices (new content type end-to-end: schema+Studio+SDK+TUI; new search retriever; new cloud site template; new theme slice) — where the GRAMMAR GAPS live: v2 has NO conditional branches, NO multi-choice/enum variables, NO FOREACH (the Doey-era DSL had one), NO command composition, NO optional op groups.

For each candidate: expressible in TODAY's grammar → author it (validated, anchors live-verified per D5, seeded per D46/D47); needs a NEW primitive → spec the primitive as a ratify-or-reject proposal with the command as motivating fixture (D3/D12/D20–D32 discipline: no primitive without a real command needing it). Deliverables: ranked candidate inventory with frequency×pain evidence; best N commands AUTHORED full-text; grammar-gap verdicts (multi-choice/enum, optional groups, composition — each ratified or rejected with reasoning); showcase/catalog updated. Rounds law: dispatcher consumes round/after natively (d38434b53) — command slices needing a new primitive are round ≥2 behind the primitive, or deferred.

Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

The finished experience: bp scaffy ls --remote grows from a 7-row proof into a working CATALOG — roughly a dozen-plus commands where every entry answers a repetition the repo can PROVE it has (≥3 historical instances in git history, a Past-Mistakes scar, or a live backlog chore). A developer's daily reflex changes: before hand-editing an accretion file, you check the catalog. And the grammar leaves the wave with an honest verdict sheet: each missing primitive either ratified with a motivating command already written against it, or rejected with the cheaper spelling that makes it unnecessary.

Lean 1 — EVIDENCE BEFORE AUTHORSHIP. The ranked inventory is the wave's spine artifact. Frequency×pain comes from three mines: git co-change clusters, memory/Past-Mistakes lore, and the open backlog. A command nobody would run twice a quarter does not get authored, however elegant.

Lean 2 — SMALL DELICATE COMMANDS ARE THE MEAT. The strongest candidates on current knowledge: add-error-shape (the query_controller+legacy_controller duplication is a documented scar — and it doubles as the FOREACH test case: if the emitter set is closed and small, explicit ops beat a loop primitive), add-canonical-marker (the @canonical planting ritual has exact syntax, a gate — docs-anchors-check §8 — and a grep-index convention), add-oban-cron-guard fix-up, add-test-fixture, ensure-import. Each is 1–3 ops, cheap to author, high frequency. These ship in round 1 in TODAY's grammar.

Lean 3 — COMPREHENSIVE COMMANDS ARE THE STRESS INSTRUMENT, not necessarily shipped verticals. Revisit add-api-route-parity (CUT in W1 for anchor reasons that marks+REANCHOR have since dissolved — the 6-anchors-3-subsystems objection needs re-testing against the W3 engine) and add-schema-type (must wrap or differentiate bp make schema). The full new-content-type vertical is attempted ON PAPER first: walk it op by op until it either fits today's grammar or names the exact primitive it dies without. That named failure IS the deliverable — it becomes the motivating fixture.

Lean 4 — GRAMMAR VERDICT PRIORS (to be tested, not assumed): ONEOF/enum variable constraint looks CHEAP and REAL (validator-level annotation in the D22 family — OPAQUE/SHAPE/SUCCESSOR precedent; add-block-type's block-family choice and add-plugin's capability set both want it); FOREACH looks REJECTABLE if every real emitter-set is closed (explicit ops are more auditable and receipt-replay stays trivial); optional op groups look REJECTABLE on house doctrine (the test is never optional here) unless a real command shows a true optional leg; command composition looks DEFERRABLE (no motivating fixture yet — the comprehensive walk decides). Conditional branches: almost certainly reject — DIRECTION+VARIANT already split polarity and flavor into separate documents, which is the scaffy way.

Lean 5 — ROUNDS HONESTY. Round 1: inventory-driven commands in today's grammar + grammar-law spec slice (if any primitive ratifies). Round 2+: commands that NEED a ratified primitive ride behind the validator/engine change, or defer to W6 entirely. Seeding + showcase update dispatch LAST (D19's lesson: the showcase embeds merged truth, never drafts).

Quality bar: every authored command meets the full W1–W4 law — DIRECTION header, marks payload-planted or VIRTUAL, guards payload-derived, ValidateFile zero findings, fmt fixpoint, anchors grep-proven with file:line evidence, seeded and tokenless-readable on guerrilla, and reversibility demonstrated (receipt replay or authored inverse). Scaffy · Wave 5 · Expand the Catalog + Stress the Grammar

Scaffy W5 — Expand the Catalog + Stress the Grammar: the wave story

IN FLIGHT: DIGEST done — 11 verifiers flying now (2 Opus worktree probes, 9 Sonnet), the LAST exploration round. Next: Decide consumes the run-proofs, files the W5 goal task + slice tasks under bp-scaffy-epic, and appends decisions here.

The wish

W1–W4 are CLOSED and LIVE: a 7-command corpus, bp scaffy validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla as command documents, reversibility proof matrix 6/6 PERFECT (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof). W5 = EXPAND THE CATALOG + STRESS THE GRAMMAR, on three axes.

(1) DISCOVERY — mine what Barkpark development ACTUALLY repeats: git-history co-change mining (files that keep co-changing with revolving siblings = injection candidates; suffix-pair co-creations; directory-shape fingerprints), the Past Mistakes / memory lore (error-shape duplication across query_controller+legacy_controller, layer-parity chores, canonical-marker planting, changeset entries, docs-currency), and the CUT backlog (scaffy-backlog-api-route-parity, scaffy-backlog-add-schema-type — revisit now that marks+REANCHOR exist).

(2) SMALL DELICATE commands — one-op precision tools a developer reaches for daily (ensure-import, add-canonical-marker, add-error-shape FOREACH-over-emitters, add-changeset, add-test-fixture…) — cheap to author, high frequency. (3) COMPREHENSIVE multi-step commands — full vertical slices (new content type end-to-end: schema+Studio+SDK+TUI; new search retriever; new cloud site template; new theme slice) — where the GRAMMAR GAPS live: v2 has NO conditional branches, NO multi-choice/enum variables, NO FOREACH (the Doey-era DSL had one), NO command composition, NO optional op groups.

For each candidate: expressible in TODAY's grammar → author it (validated, anchors live-verified per D5, seeded per D46/D47); needs a NEW primitive → spec the primitive as a ratify-or-reject proposal with the command as motivating fixture (D3/D12/D20–D32 discipline: no primitive without a real command needing it). Deliverables: ranked candidate inventory with frequency×pain evidence; best N commands AUTHORED full-text; grammar-gap verdicts (multi-choice/enum, optional groups, composition — each ratified or rejected with reasoning); showcase/catalog updated. Rounds law: dispatcher consumes round/after natively (d38434b53) — command slices needing a new primitive are round ≥2 behind the primitive, or deferred.

Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

The finished experience: bp scaffy ls --remote grows from a 7-row proof into a working CATALOG — roughly a dozen-plus commands where every entry answers a repetition the repo can PROVE it has (≥3 historical instances in git history, a Past-Mistakes scar, or a live backlog chore). A developer's daily reflex changes: before hand-editing an accretion file, you check the catalog. And the grammar leaves the wave with an honest verdict sheet: each missing primitive either ratified with a motivating command already written against it, or rejected with the cheaper spelling that makes it unnecessary.

Lean 1 — EVIDENCE BEFORE AUTHORSHIP. The ranked inventory is the wave's spine artifact. Frequency×pain comes from three mines: git co-change clusters, memory/Past-Mistakes lore, and the open backlog. A command nobody would run twice a quarter does not get authored, however elegant.

Lean 2 — SMALL DELICATE COMMANDS ARE THE MEAT. The strongest candidates on current knowledge: add-error-shape (the query_controller+legacy_controller duplication is a documented scar — and it doubles as the FOREACH test case: if the emitter set is closed and small, explicit ops beat a loop primitive), add-canonical-marker (the @canonical planting ritual has exact syntax, a gate — docs-anchors-check §8 — and a grep-index convention), add-oban-cron-guard fix-up, add-test-fixture, ensure-import. Each is 1–3 ops, cheap to author, high frequency. These ship in round 1 in TODAY's grammar.

Lean 3 — COMPREHENSIVE COMMANDS ARE THE STRESS INSTRUMENT, not necessarily shipped verticals. Revisit add-api-route-parity (CUT in W1 for anchor reasons that marks+REANCHOR have since dissolved — the 6-anchors-3-subsystems objection needs re-testing against the W3 engine) and add-schema-type (must wrap or differentiate bp make schema). The full new-content-type vertical is attempted ON PAPER first: walk it op by op until it either fits today's grammar or names the exact primitive it dies without. That named failure IS the deliverable — it becomes the motivating fixture.

Lean 4 — GRAMMAR VERDICT PRIORS (to be tested, not assumed): ONEOF/enum variable constraint looks CHEAP and REAL (validator-level annotation in the D22 family — OPAQUE/SHAPE/SUCCESSOR precedent; add-block-type's block-family choice and add-plugin's capability set both want it); FOREACH looks REJECTABLE if every real emitter-set is closed (explicit ops are more auditable and receipt-replay stays trivial); optional op groups look REJECTABLE on house doctrine (the test is never optional here) unless a real command shows a true optional leg; command composition looks DEFERRABLE (no motivating fixture yet — the comprehensive walk decides). Conditional branches: almost certainly reject — DIRECTION+VARIANT already split polarity and flavor into separate documents, which is the scaffy way.

Lean 5 — ROUNDS HONESTY. Round 1: inventory-driven commands in today's grammar + grammar-law spec slice (if any primitive ratifies). Round 2+: commands that NEED a ratified primitive ride behind the validator/engine change, or defer to W6 entirely. Seeding + showcase update dispatch LAST (D19's lesson: the showcase embeds merged truth, never drafts).

Quality bar: every authored command meets the full W1–W4 law — DIRECTION header, marks payload-planted or VIRTUAL, guards payload-derived, ValidateFile zero findings, fmt fixpoint, anchors grep-proven with file:line evidence, seeded and tokenless-readable on guerrilla, and reversibility demonstrated (receipt replay or authored inverse). The epic parent is CLOSED — Decide files a fresh W5 goal task under bp-scaffy-epic with the slice tree.

Survey plan — 15 scouts

GIT-COCHANGE-MINING — Mine git history (12+ months) for repetition evidence: which files co-change repeatedly with a revolving cast of siblings (accretion files = injection candidates)? Which suffix pairs co-create (x.go+x_test.go, x.ex+x_test.exs, migration+schema)? Which directory shapes recur (plugins/<name>/, workers/)? Rank clusters by commit count. WHY: This IS the frequency axis of frequency×pain — the ranked inventory stands on it.

ERROR-SHAPE-EMITTERS — Map the error-shape duplication scar: enumerate EVERY error emitter in api/lib (query_controller, legacy_controller, others), their exact contract shapes, whether stable anchors exist for an add-error-shape command, and exactly how many emitter sites a new error shape must touch. WHY: Decides add-error-shape's viability AND is the FOREACH test case: closed small set → explicit ops, reject FOREACH.

API-ROUTE-PARITY-REVISIT — Re-open scaffy-backlog-api-route-parity with W3+W4 eyes: re-grep the 6 anchors across router.ex/SDK/capabilities; is the manifest↔router cross-check still dead code (capabilities.ex:192)? With MARK+REANCHOR and the live engine, which of W1's cut reasons still hold? WHY: The wish explicitly orders this revisit; it is the flagship comprehensive candidate.

SCHEMA-TYPE-VS-BP-MAKE — What does bp make schema do today (flags, output, gaps)? What would add-schema-type.scaffy add — wrap it, supersede it (D15 precedent), or differentiate? Where do schema JSON files live per plugin and what accretion files reference them? WHY: Second ordered backlog revisit; also tests the command-vs-imperative-generator boundary.

CANONICAL-MARKER-CHORE — The @canonical capability marker: how many exist today (grep -rn '@canonical capability:'), what the planting ritual requires (syntax, aka:, doc:, 6-line public-def rule, §8 gate), and whether add-canonical-marker works as a command when the insertion point is 'above an arbitrary named function' rather than a fixed anchor. WHY: Tests whether today's anchor grammar can express point-at-a-symbol targets — a possible new-primitive pressure (anchor-by-pattern with a variable).

CHANGESET-FIXTURE-CHORES — What are 'changeset entries' concretely (the Changeset-gate memory: which file(s), what shape, what gate reads them)? And what repeated test-fixture patterns exist (DataCase fixtures, fixtures modules, testdata dirs, CASES arrays)? Name exact files+lines for each candidate anchor. WHY: Two wished-for small commands live or die on whether these chores have stable, markable anchors.

GRAMMAR-SEAMS — Read internal/scaffy (parse.go, validate.go, apply.go, fmt) + scaffy/README grammar law: exactly what would ONEOF/enum VARIABLE annotation, optional op groups, FOREACH, and command composition each require? Which seams are cheap (D22 annotation family) vs deep (apply/receipt semantics)? Would receipts/remove-replay survive each? Also: find the Doey-era FOREACH reference (~/github/nextgen-vscode/ng-test-example.nextgen) and record its exact semantics and known bugs. WHY: The ratify-or-reject verdicts need real cost estimates and the historical FOREACH's failure modes.

LINT-FMT-IMPACT — For each proposed primitive, which of the frozen 28 lint rules (E-001..E-020/W/P) extend or break? Is the catalog extensible without renumbering? What does fmt canonicalization do to a ONEOF list or an optional group? What new red fixtures would D30's conformance law demand? WHY: A primitive that shatters the frozen lint law costs more than its verdict paper admits — price it now.

SMALL-COMMAND-SWEEP — Sweep docs cards, Past Mistakes, memory lore, and Makefile/scripts for DAILY one-op chores beyond the named ones: docs-currency stamps, completionNouns entries, tiers.ex word-lists, .gitignore entries, crontab entries, CI workflow accretion, tag registration, capabilities flags (the file-flag-sweep backlog!). Produce 15+ candidates, each with: the accretion file, the repetition evidence, op-count estimate. WHY: Width for the ranked inventory — Digest cuts, but only from what scouts found.

COMPREHENSIVE-VERTICALS — For each wished vertical — new content type end-to-end (schema+Studio+SDK+TUI), new search retriever, new cloud site template, new theme slice — list the ACTUAL files touched by the most recent real instance in git history (e.g. how did tickets/quiz/sheets land their type? how did a retriever last get added?). For each: how many anchors, which are stable, which grammar gap it hits first. WHY: Turns 'comprehensive commands' from vision into op-by-op walkable fixtures; names the primitive each dies without.

CATALOG-SERVING-STATE — Verify the live serving loop end-to-end TODAY: bp scaffy ls --remote row count on guerrilla, seeder mechanics (scaffy/seed/main.go — what adding an 8th command requires), TAGS registration risk on publish (D47 caveat), showcase paper current block map (for the update slice), and the pull→validate→consent transcript still green. WHY: W5 ships INTO this loop; any rot found now is a round-1 fix, not a round-3 surprise.

REVERSIBILITY-OF-CANDIDATES — For the top small-command candidates (add-error-shape multi-site, add-canonical-marker, ensure-import), check the remove path: does D35/D36 receipt-replay cover them cleanly, or do multi-site same-payload ops / idempotent ensure-semantics break drift-refusal? Does 'ensure-X' (no-op if present) even fit the add/remove DIRECTION dichotomy? WHY: Reversibility is the epic's crown proof (6/6 PERFECT) — no W5 command may regress it; ensure-semantics may be a hidden primitive question.

BACKLOG-RESIDUE-TRIAGE — Read ALL open scaffy-backlog-* tasks (api-route-parity, add-schema-type, anchors-omx-exclusion, js-assert-sweep, docs-anchors-nm-prune, oban-cron-guard-gap, pnpm-assert-overbroad, bp-add-alias, file-flag-sweep, pull-drift-check, table-sparse-columns, doc-patch-file-flag) + task-920828ddf0bcc60e: which are W5 command candidates, which are plain fixes W5 should sweep, which stay parked? WHY: The wave should leave the backlog smaller, not just the catalog bigger; some backlog items ARE command candidates in disguise.

PRIOR-ART-GENERATORS — Inventory every imperative generator the repo already has (mix tasks: barkpark.plugin.new etc., bp make * verbs, seed scripts, codegen like tokens/capabilities manifests): which repetitions do they already own (scaffy must wrap or name-and-supersede per D15), and which do they do BADLY (no wiring injection) that scaffy does well? WHY: Prevents forked capability owners — house one-owner law; also surfaces command candidates hiding as half-finished mix tasks.

DISPATCHER-ROUNDS-NATIVE — Verify the claim that the dispatcher now consumes round/after fields natively (fix d38434b53): read the workflow/dispatcher code, confirm the field names and semantics a Decide plan must emit, and what happens to a round-2 slice whose round-1 dependency fails. WHY: W2 and W3 both bled on same-round fan-out; W5's plan shape must match what the dispatcher ACTUALLY parses.

Survey digest — what 15 scouts established

DISCOVERY axis, hard numbers from 12 months / 2874 commits: router.ex is the repo’s top accretion file (739 distinct co-change partners across 173 commits), followed by root.html.heex (501), content.ex (441), studio_live.ex (354), config.exs, application.exs, capabilities.ex, cli.go, types.ts. Suffix-pair co-creation: 295 commits added an .ex module WITH its _test.exs; 157 did .go/_test.go (dominated by internal/cli *_cmd.go — already covered by add-cli-verb). Commit-message corroboration: “canonical” 274 commits, “changeset” 276. Rare and already-covered: plugin registration (max pairwise co-change 5), Oban workers (10 co-adds/12mo). docs/openapi.json’s high partner count is CI churn, not a human chore.

PREMISE CORRECTION 1 — the error-shape scar is ALREADY CENTRALIZED. All 13 controllers fan into FallbackController → Barkpark.Content.Errors (errors.ex, ~35 build/1 clauses); query_controller.ex:35-44 and legacy_controller.ex:45,142 emit the SAME shared tuples, handled by one clause (errors.ex:269-305). The comments in errors.ex document that the bare-map duplication was fixed. A NEW error code touches exactly 4 manual sites (build/1 clause + @hints entry in errors.ex, docs/api-v1.md §9, errors_test.exs) — openapi.ex’s enum and error_code_coverage_test self-derive. Two scouts (co-change mining, reversibility) treated the 2-controller duplication as live pain; the direct module read wins. Consequence: add-error-shape is a closed 4-site command in TODAY’s grammar, and the wish’s FOREACH motivating fixture dissolves.
PREMISE CORRECTION 2 — the Doey-era DSL NEVER had a FOREACH. Full read of nextgen-vscode’s 698-line reference grammar file, the language server’s keyword whitelist (diagnostics.ts:57), and all 9 commits of its git history: zero DSL-level FOREACH (only JS Array.forEach in the extension’s own code). The real inherited scar is the quote-mismatch re-insert bug (charter D3c), already mechanized as E-006. FOREACH’s verdict must stand on today’s cost/benefit alone — and it does: remove/replay is 100% receipt-driven (remove.go:171 replays Receipt.Ops in reverse, never re-reads cmd.Ops), so explicit multi-site ops are independently invertible TODAY; dynamic FOREACH would break D27 (text-only validate) and D33 (static K).

Grammar-gap leans, now evidence-backed. ONEOF/enum variable: CHEAP, ratify-ready — parse.go:361-371 (EXAMPLES comma-list) is the verbatim parser template, subst.go checkShape/checkSuccessor (111-152) the runtime-check precedent, format.go’s joinFields (88-106) is keyword-agnostic so fmt is FREE, D30 bill is 1 red fixture; needs a named motivating fixture command per D22 discipline (candidates: bump-level in add-changeset, visibility in add-schema-type, tier in classify-block-type). Optional op groups: receipt/remove-SAFE by construction (skipped ops never enter the receipt; zero-mutation runs write no receipt) but the real cost is a second block-delimiter type in the parser and format.go’s 2-state fence machine — plus house doctrine (tests are never optional) and no fixture: REJECT lean holds. Composition: every engine layer is closed over ONE source file (singular Command.SourceFile; per-file mark uniqueness E-019; flat receipt schema) — receipt nesting is a schema rewrite, validation would live in the R-xxx repo-aware namespace, and no candidate needs it (add-schema-type can ASSERT the plugin exists as a precondition): DEFER. Conditionals: REJECT (DIRECTION/VARIANT already split polarity/flavor). NEW gap surfaced by the theme-slice walk: a value-capture primitive (read a token from an existing file into a VARIABLE) — real but only 2 instances, below the wave’s own 3+ bar: DEFER, name it in the verdict sheet.

Backlog revisits. add-api-route-parity: 2 of 3 D10 cut reasons hold VERBATIM at HEAD — capabilities.ex:192 still discards collect_routes (dead manifest↔router cross-check) and the 857-line contract test is hand-written per command (no auto-extend). The anchor-count worry (6 anchors / 3 subsystems) is REBUTTED by live precedent: add-block-type ships 6 IN-blocks across Go/Elixir/JS today. But plugin-owned routes AND CLI commands already auto-fold into the manifest with zero hand-edits (router/plugins.ex:177; capabilities.ex:193,230) — so the honest paths are retire-in-favor-of-plugin-register_routes or narrow to one /v1/data-zone method with the JS leg accepted as open; the original “live cross-check” acceptance bar is unmet and is a TARGET-REPO test-infra gap, not a scaffy grammar gap. That named failure is itself a wish deliverable. add-schema-type: verdict DIFFERENTIATE, not wrap — bp make schema is a pure local skeleton emitter for the ad-hoc POST /v1/schemas path, and its output shape (name/title/type:document) does NOT match plugin JSON (name/title/icon/visibility, no type key); the command’s job is the plugin-declared path: CREATE priv/plugins/<n>/schemas/*.json + register_schemas/1 wiring + test, all in today’s grammar. Caveat: tickets/quiz use inline Elixir SchemaDefinition, not JSON files — scope must say so. Correction: the direction’s “D15” cite is the add-plugin/mix-task supersession precedent; it applies to schema-type by analogy only.

New small-delicate candidates beyond the wish’s list (each with live anchors): ensure-cli-noun (3-copy drift: builtins.go:306 completionNouns is tested, the cli.go dispatch switch is D31-known, but usage.go:36 carries a THIRD, untested copy nothing ties back); ensure-cli-flag (capabilities.ex has 90 flag() calls; the missing --file class shipped as real bug #3810 and two open backlog tasks bundle with it); classify-block-type (tiers.ex @element/@widget/@section word-lists — the exact manual step charter D11 says add-block-type must never blind-MARK); add-pd-parity-entry (gen_pd_parity.ex’s @inputs map is untouched by add-block-type — a fresh, grep-proven drift gap; verify pending on whether @inputs is a hand literal); add-backfill-task (8+ Mix.Tasks share a byte-identical dry-run/--apply idiom, e.g. edges.backfill.ex:51 == paper.backfill_block_ids.ex:59 — unfiled anywhere until now); add-retriever (1 behaviour module + 1 config.exs line; registry needs zero edits). LIKELY CUT as scaffy commands: add-changeset and add-test-fixture (CREATE-only, no guarded anchor — scaffy’s MARK/REANCHOR/reversibility machinery buys nothing over a plain template; changesets also have pnpm changeset add), add-site-template (all-CREATE, 10-file stamp; discovery mechanism unverified). Tag-registry chores are live-dataset actions, not file injections — out of scaffy’s domain. No docs-currency accretion file exists (checker scripts only).

Round-0 operational facts. The INSTALLED bp binary is 89 commits stale and lacks scaffy run/remove/pull/ls entirely — make cli-build is a mandatory round-0 step or builders will misdiagnose phantom gaps. All 18 corpus tags are pre-registered on guerrilla, but ANY new tag vocabulary 422s at the publish wall (D47) — the seed slice must pre-register new tags. The charter wave-log is stale (W4 finale + seed-corpus merged after its last edit) and D43/D53 still describe manual round-sequencing — SUPERSEDED: the dispatcher natively consumes round/after since d38434b53 (buildNow = round 1; round≥2 returned as deferred_slices), but it is NOT failure-aware: a red round-1 slice does not auto-cancel its dependent round-2 — Review/lead judgment must catch orphans. (28 red fixtures, corpus zero-findings, fmt fixpoint) run fresh at HEAD; plus pin the exact ONEOF diff sites (ast.go field, parse.go case, subst.go check, format.go handling) as a concrete spec for Decide.
